source_text: Τὸ μὲν οὖν μέγεθος τῆς ἐνθάδε θλίψεως καὶ τὴν τοσαύτην τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους ὀργὴν καὶ ὅσα ὑπέμειναν οἱ μακάριοι μάρτυρες, ἐπ᾽ ἀκριβὲς οὔθ᾽ ἡμεῖς εἰπεῖν ἱκανοὶ οὔτε μὴν γραφῇ περιληφθῆναι δυνατόν. Παντὶ γὰρ σθένει ἐνέσκηψεν ὁ ἀντικείμενος, προοιμιαζόμενος ἤδη τὴν ἀδεῶς μέλλουσαν ἔσεσθαι παρουσίαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ διὰ πάντων διῆλθεν, ἐθίζων τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ καὶ προγυμνάζων κατὰ τῶν δούλων τοῦ θεοῦ, ὥστε μὴ μόνον οἰκιῶν καὶ βαλανείων καὶ ἀγορᾶς εἴργεσθαι, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ καθόλου φαίνεσθαί ἡμῶν τινα αὐτοῖς ἀπειρῆσθαι ἐν ὁποίῳ δήποτε τόπῳ.
orientation: The churches of Lyons and Vienne are writing to fellow Christians and now begin their account with the scale of the attack against them.
pass_a_gloss: So then the greatness of the affliction here and the so great anger of the pagans against the saints and as many things as the blessed martyrs endured, neither are we sufficient to say exactly nor indeed is it possible to be contained in writing. For with all strength the devil fell upon, making a prelude already of his own coming which is going to be fearlessly, and he went through all things, accustoming his own people and training them beforehand against the servants of God, so that not only to be shut off from houses and baths and market, but also in general for any one of us to appear before them was forbidden in whatever place.

choices.why: keeps servant wording of glossary for servants of Christ, applied to God

pass_b_english: We cannot tell with exactness how great the affliction is here, nor how fierce the anger of the pagans is against the saints, nor all that the blessed martyrs endured. No writing could contain it.

For the devil fell upon us with all his strength, already rehearsing his coming, which is to be without fear. He moved through every means, accustoming his own people and training them in advance against the servants of God, so that we were shut out not only from houses and baths and the marketplace, but it was forbidden for any of us to appear before them in any place at all.

last_rejected.quote: already rehearsing his coming, which is to be without fear.
last_rejected.source_quote: προοιμιαζόμενος ἤδη τὴν ἀδεῶς μέλλουσαν ἔσεσθαι παρουσίαν αὐτοῦ
last_rejected.why: The adverb ἀδεῶς ('fearlessly') modifies the coming that is about to happen. The English turns it into a garbled relative clause, so it is unclear whose fearlessness is meant.
last_rejected.fix: already preluding his coming, which will soon take place without restraint.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀδεῶς modifies μέλλουσαν ἔσεσθαι παρουσίαν, so 'his coming, which is to be without fear' keeps the adverb on the coming. The sense is intact and not misleading.
